title: GPT-6-Astra Understands Touch and Outperform Vision--Tactile--Language--Action Models
summary: Investigates whether a general-purpose multimodal model can interpret tactile feedback and use it to guide contact-rich manipulation, combining expert demonstrations, tactile references, multimodal observations, and interaction history.

title: HoloCosm: Beyond Single-Metric Benchmark Compression Across Multiple Metrics
summary: Studies multi-metric benchmark compression. HoloCosm jointly minimizes score-reconstruction error while constraining ranking distortion across 15 benchmark configurations and 85 component metrics.
figure1_caption: Figure 1: Model-ranking consistency across metrics. Each point shows Spearman ρ between rankings induced by two official metrics, all direction-aligned so higher is better. Colors show correlation ranges, the dashed line marks ρ ≥0.85, and right-side annotations give metric counts and high-correlation pairs. Weak and negative correlations are common.

title: Are We Testing Too Much? A Survey of Benchmark Compression for Efficient Evaluation of Large Language Models
summary: Surveys 119 papers on benchmark compression and organizes methods around sample selection, full-benchmark score recovery, and reliability verification.
figure1_caption: Figure 1: Publication trends in benchmark compression research from 2023 to August 2026. Quarterly and cumulative paper counts show rapid growth since 2024.

title: Right Model, Right Task: A Survey on Dynamic LLM Routing
summary: Organizes dynamic LLM routing through the information-decision boundary, covering pre-judgment, verification, and memory-based routing, alongside deployment concerns such as evaluation bias and model-pool stability.
figure1_caption: Figure 1: Publication trend of dynamic LLM routing (paper PDF).

title: Neural Chain-of-Thought Search: Searching the Optimal Reasoning Path to Enhance Large Language Models
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2026
summary: Reformulates reasoning as a dynamic search over thinking strategies. Candidate reasoning operators are evaluated with a dual-factor heuristic that balances correctness and computational cost.
figure1_caption: Figure 1: Motivation and Overview of our NCoTS. (a) Planning Bottleneck in Traditional CoT. (b) Importance of Path Planning. Sparse guiding tokens from a strong teacher significantly boost performance, confirming that path planning is the key bottleneck. (c) The NCoTS framework. Our method reformulates reasoning as a search process, employing a dual-factor heuristic to ac- tively discover paths that are both accurate and concise.

title: AngularFuse: A Closer Look at Angle-based Perception for Spatial-Sensitive Multi-Modality Image Fusion
summary: Proposes an angle-aware image-fusion framework that constrains both gradient magnitude and direction to preserve texture intensity and edge orientation.
figure1_caption: Fig. 1. We call for a closer look at angle-based perception for infrared- and visible- image fusion. The framework contains three parts. (a) Complementary Mask Generation: It takes Iir and Ivi as input and produces incomplete views Icm ir and Icm vi to force the model to borrow information from the other modality. These two views are then sent to the fusion network to obtain If. (b) Fine-Grained Reference Image Synthesis: To obtain a reliable reference, we first apply a Laplacian filter to Iir and Ivi to extract edge detail Iedge. We then blend Iedge with the high-intensity image Imax to produce Ien. Histogram equalization is applied to obtain Ieq and mitigate uneven brightness. The reference image Iref is generated by weighted fusion of Ieq and Ien with ratio α and is used to compute the reference loss Lint. (c) Angle-aware Perception: This module computes gradient magnitudes for infrared and visible images and builds a reference gradient by element-wise maximum. It then compares this reference with the gradient of the fused image If and defines two loss terms LMag and LAngle to improve structural fidelity and detail sharpness.

title: RouterEval: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Routing LLMs to Explore Model-level Scaling Up in LLMs
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2025
summary: Introduces a large-scale benchmark for LLM routing, with more than 200 million performance records across 12 evaluations and over 8,500 language models.
figure1_caption: Figure 1: The Overview of Routing LLMs. For each given input, the router distributes it to the appropriate LLM to achieve specific objectives, such as high accu- racy, low computational cost, reduced hallucinations, etc. We find that Routing LLMs is a promising paradigm for LLMs to achieve model-level scaling up.

title: Scaling Up Single Image Dehazing Algorithm by Cross-Data Vision Alignment for Richer Representation Learning and Beyond
venue: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement, 2025
summary: Studies cross-data vision alignment and self-supervised augmentation to reduce domain gaps and improve generalizable representations for single-image dehazing.
figure1_caption: Fig. 1: Comparison with state-of-the-arts in terms of flowchart and characteristics. With the rapid development of Trans- former [11], [12], the demand for data has grown at the same time. However, the simple combination of multiple datasets achieves unsatisfactory results. To address this issue, we call for the internal- and external knowledge should be further augmented by vision alignment and self-supervised learning to perform an effective large-scale training.

title: Diff-Mosaic: Augmenting Realistic Representations in Infrared Small Target Detection via Diffusion Prior
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing, 2024
summary: Introduces a diffusion-prior-based data augmentation method with pixel harmonization and diffusion enhancement to generate more realistic and diverse infrared small-target samples.
figure1_caption: Fig. 1: We compared the effects of the traditional Mosaic [1] with our method. To emphasize the diversity of samples generated by our method, we fix the top-right image of Mosaic when combining rest four images. The samples generated by the Mosaic exhibit a fragmented quality and fail to resemble a complete image. In contrast, Diff-Mosaic has a uniform distribution and coordinated grayscale. Especially in terms of the infrared small targets marked with red circles, the results of Diff-Mosaic can better enhance the diversity and realism.

title: SIRST-5K: Exploring Massive Negatives Synthesis with Self-supervised Learning for Robust Infrared Small Target Detection
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing, 2024
summary: Proposes a self-supervised negative-sample augmentation method and the SIRST-5K dataset to improve the diversity and robustness of infrared small-target detection.
figure1_caption: Fig. 1. Self-supervised strategy based on negative augmentation. To explore target correspondence in SIRST, we propose a negative augmentation approach to generate massive negatives for self-supervised representation learning.

title: MirrorDiffusion: Stabilizing Diffusion Process in Zero-shot Image Translation by Prompts Redescription and Beyond
summary: Introduces prompt redescription to align text prompts with latent codes during diffusion inversion, stabilizing structure-preserving zero-shot image translation.
figure1_caption: Fig. 1: Without any supervision, MirrorDiffusion realized three zero-shot image-to-image translations: w/o glasses →w/ glasses, Male →Female and Fox →Dog.

title: ReGeneration Learning of Diffusion Models with Rich Prompts for Zero-Shot Image Translation
summary: Explores regeneration learning for zero-shot image translation, using cross-attention guidance and cooperative updates to preserve source-image structure without additional model training.
figure1_caption: Figure 1. ReGeneration learning. In contrast to previous work, regenerative learning involves learning from the input X to a more concise representation Y ′, and subsequently learning from Y ′ to generate the ﬁnal output Y .

title: Exploring Negatives in Contrastive Learning for Unpaired Image-to-Image Translation
venue: Proceedings of the 30th ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM MM 2022)
summary: Studies whether all negative patches are necessary in contrastive learning and introduces negative pruning for unpaired image-to-image translation.
figure1_caption: Figure 1: Left: The PatchNCE loss [27]. Right: the proposed RankNCE loss. A typical patch-wise contrastive paradigms usually maximize the mutual information on all the samples, regardless of positive or negative. In comparison, RankNCE selects negative samples with good qualities based on their contribution to the mutual information (MI).
